cards.note: Never used the repository-plugins mechanism; already an npm package composed through dsh.bundle.patch into a profile.

Manifest already declares dsh.client (platform web) with exports["./client"]; no legacy dshClient field or dsh.plugin.json exists, and the profile symlinks the source manifest (no packed variant differs).
The browser half already declares dsh.client, so client-modules scans it; no dshClient-era manifest is shipped.
Every consumed service is declared in inject (host: tools/webServer/systemPrompt; client: slots); the tree contains no ctx.get call.
No optional host service is probed; the host half has no ctx.get/property-read fallback to convert.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream, so the type-vs-kind field change and the sessions-absence rule do not touch it.
The browser half is not self-rendering: it consumes only the slots service and aggregates no session state.
No task/run output tailing and no tasks.peek usage anywhere in the tree.
Already on the renamed services: injects webServer; no httpServer, tasks or onTaskDone reference remains.
The plugin neither produces nor persists ImageAttachmentRef metadata.
No read_image registration, wrapping, parsing or snapshot exists in the tree.
Not a DeepSeek LLM adapter, image interceptor, or attachment/upload cache plugin.
No Host APIProxy usage: the browser panel calls the plugin's own /tools-manager/api route, not the removed proxy.
Target is alpha.2, where A2-01 restores ignorable; the plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents either way.
No host-source patch and no import from internal session-view paths; there is no patches/ directory in the repository.
No launcher wrapper, SDK/ACP integration or direct profile-file reader; the tree ships only a bundle patch.
No headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser in the tree.
The plugin reads no tool presentation mode, PTC preset or dispatch type.
Not a permission/approval/WebFetch policy plugin; the default flip changes no plugin code path.

The documented custom /tools-manager/api/list|set route does not inherit the auth gate; the elided gateway contract now requires ctx.connection.requestRejection(req) first (403/401) and a 'connection' inject entry when the body is restored.
Not a model-provider plugin and it carries no sign-in patch, so the optional models-page capability replaces no workaround.
The plugin registers no language and carries no custom i18n patch; its tab label stays a registrant-localized slot label function.
Not a subagent orchestration or selector plugin.
Informational for deployments on the official DeepSeek adapter; no plugin-side change applies.
The plugin carries no persistent-shell or Windows directory-picker workaround to delete.
session-log-deepseek is not enabled or wrapped by this plugin.
No browser acceptance script or wrapper exists in the tree; the migration's own isolated probe nonetheless followed this card (token URL -> Cookie -> __DSH_BOOT__ entry -> advertised bundle).
The plugin registers no structured-question answerer.
Not a host UI/session-management plugin and it sets no agent-presets roots.
No TPS/first-token tracking and no isTokenDelta import.
The plugin is not a profile/bundle maintainer reusing dsh-base; it contributes one patch row to someone else's profile.
No @earendil-works/pi-ai import; not a provider/auth plugin.

The retired dsh-client-runtime type surface moved to Cordis' Context plus type-only owning-package merges (ui-renderer client for ctx.slots, ui-settings/client for the slot map entry, ui-slots for the slot base types); the package was removed from dsh.client.inject, peerDependencies and peerDependenciesMeta.

All three ids now equal the package name '@bench/dsh-bench-tools-tree': __ModuleLoader__.load id, the insert row name, and the boot entry — verified in window.__DSH_BOOT__.entries and the advertised bundle.
The plugin reads no session timeline or user-message content.
No composer DOM manipulation (draft injection, history recall, selection).
The panel renders no MarkdownText / fenced CodeBlock.
No ctx.connection.api usage; tool data arrives over the plugin's own /tools-manager/api route.
Builds no subagent seed/persisted descriptor and asserts no subagent/descriptor shape.
No ctx.workspaces navigation or directory-picker call.
The plugin persists no third-party SessionEvents, so the restored ignorable producer rule does not apply.
No ctx.remote unary call and no Remote failure handling; the browser half uses its own fetch gateway.

Added the two type owners the client source actually imports (@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer and @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings) and dropped the removed dsh-client-runtime peer; no lockfile or package manager exists in the tree to rewrite.
No CI matrix or startup wrapper forces Node 22 / skips dsh web; nothing to remove.
The plugin does not consume pluginInventory/list.
No ctx.remote.$host read; settings persistence stays host-side.
The plugin mounts none of the affected tool/agent packages itself and lists none of them as peers.
The settings namespace is the literal 'tools-manager' (lowercase + [a-z0-9-] conformant); no settingsNamespace runtime helper is imported anywhere in the tree.
